Short answer first:

- Archiving messages under the "contracts 2019" label: leaves the messages intact (not in Trash). Archiving removes the Inbox system label from each message (so they no longer show in your Inbox) but does not delete messages. If the messages still have the "contracts 2019" label, that label will still let you find them; otherwise they remain visible in All Mail and search.

- Deleting the "contracts 2019" label (from Gmail settings): removes that label from every message, but does NOT move the messages to Trash. The messages themselves remain in your account (Inbox if they still had Inbox, All Mail, or any other labels). Only the label/tag is removed.

- Deleting messages (different from deleting a label): moves the messages to Trash; after 30 days (or if you empty Trash) they are permanently deleted.

More detail / examples:
- If a message is labeled "contracts 2019" and is in your Inbox:
  - Archiving it: removes it from Inbox but it still shows under "contracts 2019" (and in All Mail).
  - Deleting the label: the message stays in Inbox (because Inbox is a separate/system label); only the "contracts 2019" tag is gone.
  - Deleting the message itself: moves it to Trash.

- If a message already only had the "contracts 2019" label (not in Inbox):
  - Archiving it has no visible effect beyond leaving it in All Mail (archive is essentially All Mail).
  - Deleting the label removes the tag; the email will still be in All Mail and searchable unless you also delete the message.

Safety note: Removing a label is reversible only by re-applying a label (you can relabel messages) — but you cannot recover messages that have been permanently deleted from Trash after 30 days (or after you manually “Delete forever”).

If you want, tell me which outcome you want (keep messages accessible but out of Inbox; remove the label but keep messages; or permanently remove the messages) and I’ll give step‑by‑step instructions for the safest method.
